feed.title: TRANCE NEXUS — Blog
feed.subtitle: Long-form trance music coverage: history, artists, labels, scene reports, gear and production guides.

entry.title: Iconic Trance Vocalists — The Voices Behind Trance's Greatest Anthems
entry.summary: Vocal trance is its own tradition within the genre. The list of vocalists whose work defined the era reads like a separate canon — one that runs parallel to the producer canon and is just as essential to understanding how the music actually sounds.

entry.title: Cosmic Gate's Anisha — The Vocalists Who Shape the Mainstage Sound
entry.summary: Cosmic Gate are nominally a two-man duo. Their post-2018 sound is unimaginable without Anisha, whose vocals and writing have shaped the duo's late career as much as their production. The pattern repeats across the genre, and crediting it changes who gets remembered.

entry.title: BT and the Stutter Edit — How One Producer Changed Music Tech
entry.summary: BT did not just make trance records — he engineered a production technique so distinctive that it eventually became a commercial software product used across pop, hip-hop, and film scoring. The story is one of the genre's most quietly consequential.

entry.title: How Tiësto Reinvented Himself — From Trance King to EDM Star Story
entry.summary: Tiësto's reinvention is the most discussed and most resented career pivot in trance history. Twenty years on, the picture is more complicated than the loyalists acknowledged at the time and more deliberate than the critics suspected.

entry.title: Building Your First Trance Playlist — 30 Essential Tracks Guide
entry.summary: A list of thirty tracks does not make you fluent in trance. But the right thirty, listened to in the right order with the right attention, gets a new listener further in a month than another year of casual sampling.

entry.title: Trance and Mental Health — The Healing Power of 138 BPM Explained
entry.summary: Many trance fans report that the music has helped them through difficult periods. The reports are consistent enough to take seriously. But the honest framing requires distinguishing what the music can do from what it cannot.

entry.title: Best Trance Festivals in Asia — Japan, India & Southeast Asia Guide
entry.summary: Asian trance festivals are not minor events. The Japanese, Indian, and Southeast Asian scenes have produced some of the largest and most musically serious trance gatherings outside Europe over the past decade.

entry.title: Above & Beyond's Group Therapy Phenomenon Explained — Complete Guide
entry.summary: Group Therapy is the most musically literate of the major trance institutions. The show, the podcast, and the live ABGT events together do something specific: they treat the trance audience as adults whose attention is worth earning.

entry.title: Anatomy of an Uplifting Trance Anthem — Section-by-Section Breakdown
entry.summary: The uplifting trance anthem is a template — a recognisable structure repeated across thousands of records. Knowing the template makes the genre much more rewarding to listen to, because you can hear what each section is asking of you.

entry.title: Top 10 Female Trance DJs You Should Know in 2026 — Definitive List
entry.summary: Lists are reductive but useful as starting points. These ten women are doing the most interesting work in trance DJing right now, and any one of their 2026 sets is a faster education than reading another think piece.

entry.title: Why Trance Music is Having a Renaissance in 2026 — Revival Analysed
entry.summary: Trance is more visible in 2026 than it has been since 2010. The question is whether the resurgence is structural — driven by something genuinely new — or a nostalgia cycle that will fade.

entry.title: Trance Fashion History — From Rave Wear to Festival Couture Guide
entry.summary: Every era of trance has had a recognisable visual signature. The neon-and-UV rave wear of the late 90s, the all-black mainstage uniform of the mid-2000s, and the high-production festival couture of the 2020s tell their own version of the genre's history.

entry.title: Armin van Buuren's A State of Trance — 25 Years of Influence Story
entry.summary: A State of Trance is no longer just a radio show. Twenty-five years in, it functions as the genre's tastemaking institution — a weekly broadcast that has done more to shape what counts as trance than any single record or producer.

entry.title: How to Listen to Trance Music — Complete Beginner's Listening Guide
entry.summary: Trance is not a genre you grasp from a thirty-second clip. The format rewards listeners who give it the time and attention it asks for, and the gap between casual and committed listening is unusually wide.

entry.title: Women Trance Producers — Studio Architects Who Shaped the Genre
entry.summary: Trance's mainstream story has historically been told through male DJ names. The producer history is different — women have been writing and producing the records all along, and the genre has been quietly shaped by their work for thirty years.

entry.title: Trance Music's Influence on Pop, Hip-Hop & Other Genres Today
entry.summary: Trance has had a much wider musical influence than the genre's mainstream profile would suggest. Many of the techniques pop producers now reach for — supersaw leads, breakdown-and-drop dynamics, atmospheric pads — are trance imports.

entry.title: Best Trance Music Documentaries — Definitive Watchlist for Fans
entry.summary: The serious documentary record on trance music is smaller than the genre deserves, but the films that exist are essential viewing for any committed fan.

entry.title: Trance and Meditation — Music for Mind Expansion & Focus Guide
entry.summary: Trance is not literally meditation music — but the structural similarities are real, and many fans use the music as part of a meditation or focus practice. The overlap rewards careful attention.

entry.title: The Spirituality of Trance Music — Why It Hits Different in 2026
entry.summary: Ask any serious trance fan to describe their best night and the words "spiritual" or "religious" arrive within minutes. This is not a casual analogy. The music does something specific to the listener that demands serious vocabulary.

entry.title: Trance Music in Films and TV — Memorable Moments & Soundtrack Guide
entry.summary: Film and television have used trance music — and trance-adjacent electronic textures — to score some of the most emotionally charged moments in recent screen history. The pairing works because both forms understand catharsis.

entry.title: Female Trance DJs Reshaping the Scene in 2026 — Top Producers
entry.summary: In 2026, the most important question about women in trance is not whether they are present — they are — but what their continued prominence means for the future shape of the genre.

entry.title: New Generation Trance Artists to Watch in 2026 — Top Producer Picks
entry.summary: Every era of trance has had artists who arrived early enough that listeners can claim they were paying attention before things got big. These are the names worth knowing in 2026.

entry.title: Miss Monique — Biography, Best Tracks & Progressive House Rise
entry.summary: Miss Monique's rise from a Kyiv DJ uploading mixes to YouTube to one of the most-followed progressive DJs in the world is one of the genre's most distinctive 2020s success stories.

entry.title: Nifra — Biography, Best Tracks & Coldharbour Tech-Trance Queen
entry.summary: Nifra is one of the most consistently exciting DJs in modern trance — a tech-trance specialist whose sets reliably outwork most headliners on a festival bill.

entry.title: A State of Trance Turns 25: The Show That Defined a Genre
entry.summary: A State of Trance turned twenty-five in 2026. From a 2001 launch on ID&T Radio to a weekly Thursday broadcast reaching tens of millions across 150+ stations in 84 countries, ASOT has become the institutional centre of trance music — and the Rotterdam Ahoy anniversary marks the moment.

entry.title: Women in Trance — Pioneers, Producers & Modern Stars Complete Guide
entry.summary: Trance has had women at its centre since the beginning. The story of those women — pioneers, vocalists, DJs, producers, label heads — is one of the genre's most under-told stories.

entry.title: Trance Revival 2026: Why the Genre Is Back and What's Driving It
entry.summary: In 2026, trance is back on festival main stages and inside the wider conversation around dance music. Five intersecting forces are driving the return — none of them decisive alone, but together producing a shift that looks structural rather than seasonal.

entry.title: Trance Tracks That Defined Each Decade — Retrospective Top List
entry.summary: If you had to play one trance record to explain each decade of the genre to someone, which would you choose? This is the disciplined version of that thought experiment.

entry.title: Modern Trance Classics 2020s — Definitive Records of the Decade
entry.summary: It is too early to write a definitive 2020s ranking — the decade is half over. But certain records released since 2020 have already been absorbed into the genre's shared memory.

entry.title: Best Trance Tracks of the 2010s — The Definitive Decade Guide
entry.summary: The 2010s could have been the decade trance disappeared. Instead, it was the decade trance learned how to share a stage with EDM, deep house, and pop — without losing what makes it itself.

entry.title: Best Trance Anthems of the 2000s — Definitive Top Tracks Guide
entry.summary: If the 1990s built trance's vocabulary, the 2000s wrote the genre's most-quoted sentences. The decade gave us the anthems that still close festival sets twenty years later.

entry.title: Best Trance Tracks of the 1990s — The Definitive Top List Guide
entry.summary: The 1990s did not just give trance its first hits. It built the entire language the genre would speak for the next thirty years — and most of those records still sound enormous on a real club system.

entry.title: Underground Trance Scene 2026 — Boutique Labels & Events Guide
entry.summary: The most exciting developments in trance often happen away from the main stage. The underground scene is where the music's future is being written — and it's more vibrant than ever.

entry.title: Ibiza and Trance — Complete Love Story from Cafe del Mar to Today
entry.summary: Ibiza gave trance some of its most iconic moments. The island's distinctive atmosphere — sunset, sea, the mingling of nationalities — amplifies trance's emotional power to something almost mythical.

entry.title: Tomorrowland Trance Stage — A Sacred Ground for Trance Music
entry.summary: Tomorrowland is the world's biggest music festival. For trance fans, its dedicated stage is something more — a gathering point where the genre is celebrated at the highest possible level.

entry.title: A State of Trance — The Radio Show That Changed Trance Music
entry.summary: A State of Trance is not just a radio show. It is a weekly ritual, a global community, and the most important institution in trance music history.

entry.title: Best Trance Clubs in Europe — Amsterdam, Berlin, London & More
entry.summary: Europe remains the heartland of trance club culture. These are the venues where the music has always been taken most seriously — and where it still sounds best.

entry.title: Ferry Corsten — Biography, Best Tracks & Three Decades of Trance
entry.summary: Ferry Corsten's career spans every era of trance music. From System F's "Out of the Blue" to his latest releases, innovation has always been his signature.

entry.title: Tiësto's Evolution — From Trance God to EDM Superstar Biography
entry.summary: No artist in electronic music has undergone a more dramatic evolution than Tiësto. His journey from trance deity to global EDM superstar is a story about music, money, and identity.

entry.title: The 50 Best Progressive Trance Tracks of All Time — Definitive List
entry.summary: Progressive trance is the genre's longest-form subgenre — patient, harmonically generous, structurally sophisticated. This is the canon that runs from BT and Sasha in the 1990s to Tinlicker and Cristoph today, ranked with reasons.

entry.title: The 50 Best Psytrance Tracks of All Time — Goa to Modern Full-On
entry.summary: Psytrance is the genre's most self-contained subculture — its own festivals, labels, visual aesthetic, and listening community largely separate from mainstream trance. This is the canon that runs from 1990s Goa beach parties to today's Boom and Ozora mainstages, ranked with reasons.

entry.title: Best Trance Tracks of May 2026 — ASOT 2026 Compilation & H1 Wrap
entry.summary: May 2026 closes the first half of the year with the long-awaited ASOT 2026 compilation, mixed by Armin van Buuren across three discs (Pulse / Frequency / Energy) — a 25-year anniversary statement that consolidates the year's most-played material into a single release moment.

entry.title: The 100 Best Trance Tracks of All Time — Definitive Ranked List 2026
entry.summary: Picking the all-time best trance tracks is a thirty-year argument with no settled ending. This list is our editorial answer for 2026 — fifty records that earn their place across the canon, each verified against the historical record and ranked with reasons.

entry.title: The 50 Best Uplifting Trance Tracks of All Time — Definitive Ranked List
entry.summary: Uplifting trance is the genre's most misunderstood subgenre — written off by outsiders as cheesy, defended by insiders as the most emotionally direct music dance culture has produced. This is our ranked answer to which records earn permanent place in that argument.

entry.title: The 50 Best Vocal Trance Tracks of All Time — Definitive Songs Guide
entry.summary: Vocal trance is the genre's songwriter tradition — the records where the human voice carries the emotional load that the synthesizer alone cannot. This is the canon from Robert Miles' "One and One" through HALIENE's late-2010s catalogue, ranked with reasons.

entry.title: Paul van Dyk — Biography, Best Tracks & Influence on Trance Music
entry.summary: Paul van Dyk did not just play trance — he helped create it. From East Berlin to global stages, his story is one of music, politics, and perseverance.

entry.title: What is Balearic Trance? — Sun, Sea & Slow BPM Definitive Guide
entry.summary: Balearic trance is the sun-soaked, slower end of the genre — rooted in Ibiza's Café del Mar sunset-bar tradition, codified by Energy 52's "Café del Mar" (1993) and Chicane's late-90s catalogue, and built around the Mediterranean evening / sunrise emotional palette.

entry.title: What is Dream Trance? — From Robert Miles to Today Definitive Guide
entry.summary: Dream trance is the piano-led, melancholic Italian subgenre that crystallised in 1995-96 around Robert Miles' "Children" and the surrounding Media Records / DBX catalogue — the moment when trance briefly became Europe's biggest pop format.

entry.title: What is Goa Trance? — Origins, Sound & Pioneers Definitive Guide
entry.summary: Goa trance is the original psychedelic trance form — the 1989–1995 Goa beach-party scene where Western travellers, Indian local culture, and the new digital studio technology of the early 1990s combined into a sound that all later psytrance directly descends from.

entry.title: What is Hard Trance? — Energy, BPM & Classic Anthems Guide
entry.summary: Hard trance is the aggressive, peak-time end of the genre — faster, harder-kicked, and more rave-oriented than uplifting trance, descended from late-1990s Belgian and German rave culture and the parent form of modern hardstyle.

entry.title: What is Progressive Trance? — Complete Guide to the Sound
entry.summary: Progressive trance is the patient, atmospheric counterpart to uplifting — slower, deeper, and built on long-form arrangement principles where mood and texture develop gradually over many bars rather than crashing into a peak-time release.

entry.title: What is Psytrance? — From Goa to Modern Full-On Definitive Guide
entry.summary: Psytrance is the psychedelic offshoot of trance — high-tempo, rolling-bass-driven, surreal in sound design, and culturally a parallel universe to mainstream trance with its own festivals, labels, and listener community.

entry.title: What is Tech Trance? — The Tougher Side of the Genre Guide
entry.summary: Tech trance is the rhythm-forward end of the genre — where trance's long-form arrangement meets techno-influenced kick and bass programming, the lead synth is de-emphasised, and the body of the track is carried by drive rather than melody.

entry.title: What is Trance Music? — Complete Guide to the Genre & Sound
entry.summary: Trance is a melody-driven electronic dance genre that emerged in early-1990s Germany and Benelux. The defining traits are a steady 130–145 BPM pulse, long arrangements built around hypnotic synth motifs, and the breakdown-and-buildup architecture that produces the euphoric release the genre is named for.

entry.title: What is Uplifting Trance? — Sound, History & Key Artists Guide
entry.summary: Uplifting trance is the most emotionally explicit subgenre of trance — designed to deliver moments of euphoric release through soaring lead synths, major-key chord progressions, and breakdowns that build to enormous, cathartic climaxes.

entry.title: What is Vocal Trance? — Definition, Sound & Top Artists Guide
entry.summary: Vocal trance is the songwriter tradition inside trance — the form where a sung human voice carries the emotional weight that the lead synth carries in instrumental trance, and where verse-chorus arrangement replaces the breakdown-and-drop architecture of the rest of the genre.

entry.title: Above & Beyond — Biography, Anjunabeats Empire & Iconic Tracks
entry.summary: Above & Beyond did not just make music — they built a movement. The Anjuna story is one of the most remarkable in electronic music history.

entry.summary: Five times number one DJ in the world. Host of the most-listened-to dance radio show in history. For millions of fans, Armin van Buuren is not just a DJ — he is the living definition of trance.

entry.summary: Trance has outlasted dozens of trends and survived the rise and fall of EDM's commercial peak. What makes this music so durable? The answer goes deeper than sound.

entry.summary: In a genre built on synthesisers and machinery, the human voice carries a special power. Vocal trance has produced some of the most beloved music of the past three decades.

entry.summary: Psytrance is more than a genre — it's a lifestyle, a philosophy, and a global subculture. Its journey from Goa's beaches to the world stage is one of electronic music's most extraordinary stories.

entry.summary: Trance music's journey from Frankfurt's underground clubs to a global cultural phenomenon is one of electronic music's greatest stories — spanning three decades and every continent.

Push returned with "Back When We Believed" on Pure Trance NEON, FSOE Argento debuted with the Ron / Leeds collaboration, and the Anjuna release calendar continued the year's steady drip of Above & Beyond singles.

entry.title: Best Trance Tracks of February 2026 — ASOT 25 Anthem & Top Picks
entry.summary: February 2026 was the ASOT 25 month: Armin van Buuren, Richard Durand, and Dicosis dropped the official ELEVATION anthem, Aly & Fila reactivated their Jwaydan vocal partnership for FSOE, and the festival's two-night Rotterdam edition turned the month into the year's most-anticipated trance event so far.

entry.title: Best Trance Tracks of January 2026 — Top 10 Picks of the Month
entry.summary: January 2026 opened the year on a high note: Above & Beyond delivered four new singles in a single Anjunabeats drop, Paul van Dyk reunited with Ciaran McAuley on Black Hole, and the Raw / Deep / Hypnotic wing of Beatport's chart kept producing the kind of lower-tempo material that the previous twelve months made the genre's most-watched space.
